items.title: AI Agents and Non-Human Identities: The Security Risks and How to Reduce Them
items.description: The rise of AI in enterprises has expanded the attack surface. Learn how GitGuardian can help you secure non-human identities and prevent unauthorized access.

items.title: Your AI Coding Agent Just Leaked a Secret. Bots Found It on Docker Hub in 8 Seconds
items.description: Bots used AWS keys planted in Docker Hub images within 7.86 seconds. AI coding agent config files are now carrying real secrets into those same layers, because .gitignore does not apply to a Docker build. Here are five fixes, from .dockerignore to stopping the leak at the agent.

items.title: Never Let the Model See the Secret: Zero Data Retention Is Not Enough
items.description: Nearly 2 million bait prompts. Three breached AI providers. Stolen AWS keys tested within hours. Dragos showed that Zero Data Retention is a promise, not a control. Here is how to stop secrets on the laptop, before any model sees them.

items.title: How to Benchmark Secret Detection Vendors Without Fooling Yourself: 8-Step Guide
items.description: Comparing secrets detection tools sounds simple: run each on the same data and count findings. In practice, the dataset, matching rules, and labeling method can each flip the result. Here’s a vendor-neutral method to benchmark secret scanning tools fairly.

items.title: What Five Months of the Enterprise Good Samaritan Program Taught Us
items.description: We found 1,588 companies leaked credentials. 62% of the valid ones still worked, and only 35% of companies we emailed replied.

items.title: React2STEAL: Hijacked GitHub Accounts Exploit React2Shell and Publish Stolen Secrets
items.description: React2STEAL uses GitHub Actions in hijacked accounts to exploit React2Shell (CVE-2025-55182) on Next.js servers, then commits stolen environment variables, cloud keys, and AI API keys to public repositories. Patch, then revoke every secret the server could reach.

items.title: The Fireworks AI Breach: How One Vendor Key Became a Supply Chain Attack on Cursor
items.description: A breach at Fireworks AI exposed a read-only key Cursor had issued to it. The attacker used it to copy agent traces, found more credentials inside, and planted trojanized Claude Code builds in Cursor’s marketplace cache. Here’s how the credential chain worked, and what AppSec should change.

items.title: Financial Services Cybersecurity vs. ARTEX: Credentials in Plain Sight
items.description: Microsoft says Storm-3358 has used ARTEX against financial institutions since October 2026. GitGuardian found secrets in 6.9% of active finance-linked public GitHub repositories in 2025, and at least 446 sensitive secrets were still valid when first detected.

items.title: Java4Shell: When Decoding base64 Leads to RCE
items.description: On November 17, 2026, OpenJDK and Oracle fixed Java4Shell. It may allow pre-auth RCE under default configurations. Exploitation was confirmed on identity, CI/CD, artifact repository, and collaboration applications. This kind of Java application stores credentials, so it can be a secret-theft vector.

items.title: How to Handle Secrets in Python: Six Secure Patterns
items.description: DevOps engineers must handle secrets with care. In this series, we summarize best practices for leveraging secrets with your everyday tools.

items.title: AI-Powered Attacks Go Autonomous: Start With Credentials
items.description: Fully autonomous cyberattacks may be only months away. The incidents happening right now show exactly where defenders should focus their attention.

items.title: What the ARTEX FBI Alert Means for Credential Security
items.description: The FBI’s ARTEX alert shows AI agents reaching privileged access in under three hours, while leaked credentials stay valid for years. Here’s what that gap means for defenders and how to close it.

items.title: Why We Built the Good Samaritan Program
items.description: The first thing GitGuardian ever shipped was a free warning. Now we’re making sure it gets heard.

items.title: Why Is Credential Rotation So Hard? Follow One Leaked Production Key
items.description: A leaked production key had copies in code, config, a pipeline, a vault and Jira. Follow the credential rotation twice, once by hand over 3 days and once with a full inventory in hours.

items.title: A Valid Signature Isn’t Enough: Attributing and Validating Leaked JWTs
items.description: During a six-month internship with the GitGuardian security research team, Florent Leroy built the attribution rules and live checkers described in this post. Since Aug. 5, they run in production.
